NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhaka’s extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being legally examined, so New Delhi could not state a deadline for her return.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” High commissioner Dinesh Trivedi remarked during a discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. PTI reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.Hasina sought asylum in India after a massive anti-establishment agitation led to the collapse of her government in August 2024.Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasina’s extraction. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through a Bangladeshi aircraft.“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said.Trivedi alleged the situation emerged because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world.“What was our choice?” Trivedi asked, pointing at the uncertainty of the potential situation, had India denied entry to Hasina’s aircraft.India-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi.Hasina was replaced by an interim government led by Mohammad Yunus, which repeatedly called for her extraction from India.During that 18-month interim rule, Hasina was tried in absentia by a special tribunal and sentenced to death; her Awami League party was also disbanded.Following the February 12 elections, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) came to power. Its government endorsed the ban on Hasina's party and repeatedly renewed the demand for her extradition.However, relations never fully recovered despite a new government in Bangladesh.They were strained further when Hasina addressed a virtual press conference from New Delhi on 5 August 2026, the second anniversary of her removal from power. Bangladesh's foreign ministry had earlier said that the atmosphere for Rahman's visit had been "vitiated" by Hasina's virtual press interaction.India has maintained that it had no role in the media event and that it does not endorse anything said at the forum about the Bangladesh government.Rahman had declined the invitation to attend the BRICS outreach summit, while a separate bilateral invitation has been on hold since February.Despite the downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, said after meeting Trivedi on Tuesday that Dhaka was "positive" about progress in discussions on Rahman's proposed visit to India; PTI reported that no date has been fixed yet.
Article Summary: India-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through an aircraft. Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasina’s extraction.

Article Title: Teaching is just the start: The crushing burden on India's college teachers
Article Text:
According to a survey on higher education, while recommended student-teacher ratio (STR) targets in higher education range between 15:1 and 20:1, the national average hovers between 24:1 and 27:1.

Modern classroom: More than academics

When attendance collide with career

Teacher becomes institutional buffer

When personal problems enter classroom

Counselling gap, a stigma problem

Emotional burden on teachers

Beyond the classroom

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a brightly lit classroom at an engineering college in Bengaluru, a fourth-year Computer Science lecture is underway. At the front, a professor moves through a technical lesson while also keeping track of attendance sheets and administrative requirements.In the middle rows, a student sits quietly, mentally calculating train schedules between Bengaluru and Pune. He is trying to work out how to explain to a corporate employer that a career-launching Pre-Placement Offer (PPO) could be at risk because of a mandatory offline attendance requirement for a single elective subject.The scene captures a growing tension inside India’s higher education system.For final-year students, college is no longer only about completing a degree. With competition for jobs intensifying, students are increasingly focused on internships, practical skills, early employment and mental health support. But the institutional framework around them remains tied to attendance thresholds, credit requirements, standardised evaluation and administrative compliance.Caught at the centre of these competing pressures is the college teacher.According to data from the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), while recommended Student-Teacher Ratio (STR) targets in higher education range between 15:1 and 20:1, the national average hovers between 24:1 and 27:1.In public and state institutions, that figure can rise to 35:1 or 50:1, with individual undergraduate lectures accommodating 80 to 120 or more students per section.The pressure is compounded by faculty shortages. Central universities report faculty vacancy rates between 29% and 34%, while senior professor vacancies frequently exceed 50%. Across technical institutions such as the IITs, NITs and IIITs, unfilled positions range from 30% to over 50%.This leaves teachers performing several roles at once: academic instructors, institutional policy enforcers, career advisers and, often, informal listeners when students are struggling.At the same time, they have to manage UGC Academic Performance Indicators, NAAC and NIRF documentation and heavy teaching loads.For today's students, particularly those in their final year, the classroom is closely linked to the question of what happens after graduation.“A student may come because he is confused about an internship, worried about placements or simply doesn't know how to deal with something happening at home. We try to listen, but there is a limit to what a subject teacher can realistically handle,” Prakash, a college faculty member at an engineering college, says.From the student's perspective, the final year can feel like a race against time, with academic requirements running alongside internships, placements and preparations for entering the workforce.Pranav Vats, a final-year Computer Science and Engineering student in Bengaluru, describes what students prioritise:“Whenever a guy comes to a college, he eventually wants to get placed. He doesn't want to get a 9-plus CGPA every semester. He just wants to get placed in a good company and do well in his career financially and also growth-wise... I have been doing internships from the first year itself. And whatever interviews I have been going through, nobody asked me about what my CGPA is. Everybody just asked, okay, how much do you know, how much practical skills you have, and how well you understand the market and how well do you understand your business in which you are going to work now. ”That shift creates a difficult balance for teachers. Students may see practical experience as more directly connected to employment, while faculty members remain responsible for ensuring that students complete prescribed courses, credits and attendance requirements.The tension becomes particularly visible during placement and internship season.Pranav describes a situation in which he had secured an internship opportunity in Pune after clearing an interview:“Two, three months back, I got an interview. I've cleared it. I went to Pune. And at that time, I got permission from college. They gave me this letter of acknowledgement that you can go and pursue your six months internship, and all. But all of a sudden, after two months, they are saying that no, you have to fulfil your academic requirements and all... This company is very good. I'm doing very well there. And they are giving me the PPO for it. I could have got placed. But right now, this company is not giving away. College is saying that you have to attend weekly once class. As a student, it is not possible for me to come from Pune to Bangalore every week to attend some stupid class that is not even relevant to my coursework, which is not even relevant to my computer science degree... It is just an open elective subject.”He says discussions with his mentor, department head and other authorities did not resolve the problem. Pranav says similar situations have affected other students, including those with jobs or internships in Bengaluru itself.He says, “A guy got placed in Bangalore itself. And he said, ‘Sir, I can't attend this class this week because I've got placed.’ They said, ‘You have to fulfill this academic thing’.”For teachers, however, understanding the student's situation does not necessarily mean being able to change the rule.“The final year is particularly difficult because everything seems to happen at once. Students are completing projects, dealing with attendance and examinations, and at the same time worrying about placements and what they are going to do after graduation. You can see that pressure building up, especially when a student's plans don't work out,” the faculty said.The faculty member explains the dilemma, “There are situations where a student gets an internship or an opportunity outside the college and genuinely needs flexibility. As a teacher, you may understand why that opportunity matters to him. But you are also responsible for implementing the academic requirements. That can put the teacher in an uncomfortable position because you may sympathise with the student without having the authority to change the rule. ”The teacher is therefore often caught between three sets of expectations.The administration expects attendance, syllabus completion and documentation for institutional requirements. Students expect empathy, career guidance and flexibility. Parents expect academic performance, safety and career outcomes.The teacher may have to explain an institutional decision to a student without having any authority over that decision.“Sometimes the student is upset with the institution, the parents are worried about the student's performance and the department is concerned about academic requirements,” the teacher explains. “The teacher ends up sitting in the middle. We are expected to explain one side to the other, even though we may not have control over the decision ourselves.”For students, this can reinforce the perception that teachers are primarily there to enforce attendance and award marks.Pranav puts it bluntly, “They don't care, they just want these things to attend classes, they want attendance, they want marks, that's it... If you go to an off-campus thing, where majorly everybody is applying right now, nobody asks you about your CGPA. They just want you to have your practical skills. But this CGPA thing or whatever coursework they are teaching us in college, it is not even relevant to what we will work in our offices. ”The pressure is not limited to academics and placements.Teachers are also increasingly expected to recognise when students are struggling emotionally, even though they may not be trained to provide professional mental health support.“You spend enough time with a class to notice changes,” the faculty member observes. “If a student who is normally interactive suddenly stops speaking, misses classes or stops submitting work, you notice it. The difficult part is deciding whether to ask, ‘Is everything okay?’ because you don't know whether the student wants you to enter that part of his life,” Prakash say.The teacher describes the boundary involved, “There is a very fine line between being concerned about a student and becoming intrusive. If I ask too many questions, it may seem intrusive. If I don't ask anything, I may miss something important. Teachers are constantly trying to judge where that line is.”At the same time, faculty members recognise their own limitations.“I want my students to know that they can approach me, but I also have to be honest about my limitations. I can listen, I can help them think through a problem and I can direct them towards the right person. But I am not trained to provide therapy, and pretending otherwise can be harmful,” Prakash says.Many institutions have counselling cells or mentor-mentee systems, but having a service does not necessarily mean students will use it.Pranav says his mentor-mentee system is largely focused on academic issues:“For every 20 or 30 sets of people there is assigned one mentor. So whatever the issues you have regarding the college, you can talk with them and they can get a resolution about it... [But] there is nothing like that through which we can discuss our career... They are strictly for the subject.”He says students also face peer pressure around seeking counselling.“We have one basically like they have hired a person... if you have any emotional issues or something like that, then you can go schedule a session,” Pranav says. “[But] if you suppose you go to a counsellor there is this peer pressure. If you go to a counselor, or maybe you're discussing things with the teacher, you would seem like a weak person.”“This thing is very very disturbing to the students and nobody talks about it because everybody feels that okay, if I talk about it I can feel weak about it and people will think that okay he's not mature enough to deal with his own problem on his own... I talk to some of my friends about it who are eventually on the same path... but majorly I work with my pressure on my own,” Pranav adds.When behaviour changes significantly, teachers also have to balance intervention with confidentiality.“If I feel that a student's behaviour has changed significantly, I cannot just say, ‘That's his personal matter.’ There are situations where you have to involve the appropriate support system. But you also have to be careful about confidentiality and about not turning a student's difficulty into a public issue,” Prakash says.While student stress receives increasing attention, the pressure on faculty can remain largely invisible.A teacher managing a class of 80 to 120 students may also have to deal with staff shortages, administrative work, evaluations, meetings and institutional documentation. A difficult conversation with a student does not necessarily end when the class does.The faculty member says teachers need institutional support if they are expected to take on these additional responsibilities.Prakash says, “I don't think teachers are unwilling to take on a larger role. Most teachers care about what happens to their students. But if the expectation is that we should identify emotional distress, provide career guidance, handle academic problems and support students through personal crises, then the institution also has to give teachers training and a proper support structure.”The experiences of both students and teachers point to a larger structural problem.When colleges rely on individual teachers to enforce academic rules, handle administrative requirements, guide students through careers and respond to emotional distress, the teacher becomes the point where multiple pressures meet.The solution therefore cannot rest entirely on individual faculty members.As colleges respond to changing job markets and rising student pressures, the system would require clearer boundaries for faculty responsibilities, greater flexibility for final-year students navigating legitimate career opportunities, and stronger professional support systems.For the teacher standing at the front of the classroom, the challenge is no longer simply teaching the subject. It is managing everything that happens around it, often without the authority, time or institutional support required to do so.
Article Summary: For final-year students, college is no longer only about completing a degree. With competition for jobs intensifying, students are increasingly focused on internships, practical skills, early employment and mental health support. Caught at the centre of these competing pressures is the college teacher.

Article Title: From ‘tareekh pe tareekh’ to justice within 3 years: Amit Shah hails BNS, overhaul of criminal laws
Article Text:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah addresses the 'Gopalak Sammelan', at BHEL Dussehra Ground, in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday said the full implementation of India’s new criminal laws would enable cases to be disposed of within three years, from the filing of an FIR to the Supreme Court.“India’s judicial system was once known for its ‘tareekh pe tareekh’ taunts, but now, with the full implementation of the new criminal laws, justice will be delivered within three years, from the filing of an FIR to the Supreme Court,” he said.Shah was addressing the conference after inaugurating an exhibition on the new criminal laws at Dussehra Ground in Bhopal’s BHEL area.The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) came into effect on July 1, 2024. Shah said the laws incorporate science and technology into forensic investigations and include provisions concerning women’s safety, mob lynching, missing children and terrorism.He said the laws enacted under British rule were intended to preserve that rule, while the new laws were designed to protect the “honour, property, and body of Indian citizens”.“The fundamental principle of these laws is justice, not punishment.The provision of punishment is only to deter criminals from committing crimes. After the full implementation of these laws, our criminal justice system will be among the most modern in the world,” Shah said.Shah also said the government was working on a detailed plan to ensure drug abuse becomes non-existent in Madhya Pradesh after December 31, 2029.Turning to the cooperative sector, Shah attacked the Congress alleging that since Independence, poeple involved in agriculture, rural development, and cooperatives had been demanding a separate ministry, but the then-ruling party “prevented the establishment of such a ministry for 75 years”.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi has given a new direction to the cooperative sector by establishing a separate Ministry of Cooperation. Our cowherds will benefit the most from this. Middlemen take a large share of the profit when milk is sold in the open market, but there is no place for them in the cooperative model,” he said.At the event, the foundation stone was laid for a Rs 255-crore milk processing plant in Ujjain, with a capacity of three lakh litres per day. Officials also said an MoU had been exchanged between KRIBHCO and the Madhya Pradesh State Biodiversity Board to develop an urban forest in Bhopal under the Morvan Project.
Article Summary: Shah was addressing the conference after inaugurating an exhibition on the new criminal laws at Dussehra Ground in Bhopal’s BHEL area. Shah said the laws incorporate science and technology into forensic investigations and include provisions concerning women's safety, mob lynching, missing children and terrorism.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”

Article Title: ‘Beating his drum away’: Congress targets PM Modi for ‘ignoring’ rising inflation in Mann Ki Baat
Article Text:
Cong targets PM Modi for 'ignoring' inflation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
Article Summary: The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat. “The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away,” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote.

Stock markets tumbled on Monday, with the benchmark Sensex plunging over 1,100 points to a six-month low and the Nifty closing below 22,800 as surging crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and weak global trends weighed on investor sentiment.The 30-share BSE Sensex tanked 1,124.02 points, or 1.52 per cent, to settle at 72,771.72, its lowest closing level since March 30, 2026. During the session, it fell as much as 1,179.51 points, or 1.59 per cent, to 72,716.23.The market rout wiped out over Rs 6 lakh crore off the value of BSE-listed firms, whose combined market capitalisation stood at around Rs 476 lakh crore.Crude oil prices remained a key factor driving the benchmarks. Brent crude futures rose 1.5% to around $106 a barrel, while Asian markets declined 0.2%.Oil prices have remained volatile since late February, when the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran, triggering a war in the Middle East. Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have also continued for the seventh consecutive month. The latest rise in crude prices came amid a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks.Earlier, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the confict.Meanwhile, Iran, maintained that diplomacy was the only way to resolve its conflict with the United States and Israel.The movement in crude prices remains particularly important for India, the world’s third-largest crude importer. Any progress on a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz could ease energy prices and provide some relief to India's import bill and the rupee, while renewed geopolitical tensions could keep volatility elevated," Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking, said.On the domestic front, Mishra said industrial production data for August and the HSBC manufacturing PMI reading would be released during the week. On the global front, US consumer confidence, JOLTS job openings and the eurozone’s September inflation cluster will be watched for signals on expectations around the global rate cycle.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $35,000 donation takes spotlight as his $3.4M foundation faces scrutiny
Article Text:

Travis Kelce directs $35,000 prize to Operation Breakthrough

Eighty-Seven and Running faces scrutiny over its finances

Earlier this year, Travis Kelce’s charitable work drew fresh attention after he won the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Charity Challenge for the third time. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end secured a $35,000 donation, but instead of directing the money to his own foundation, Eighty-Seven and Running, he chose Kansas City nonprofit Operation Breakthrough. The decision came as his foundation faced questions over its financial reporting, governance and spending. The move put the focus not only on Kelce’s latest charitable contribution, but also on how athlete-led foundations manage money and maintain public trust.Kelce won the 2025 Charity Challenge through a social media vote, finishing ahead of Buffalo Bills offensive lineman Dion Dawkins and Philadelphia Eagles tackle Jordan Mailata. His prize will support Operation Breakthrough, an organisation Kelce has worked with since his rookie season in 2015.The choice also carries added significance because Taylor Swift recently donated $250,000 to the Kansas City nonprofit. Operation Breakthrough supports children and families facing poverty through education, emergency assistance and other programmes.Unlike Kelce’s foundation, Operation Breakthrough has a long-established structure.Its latest available tax records show that it spent about 83 cents of every dollar on charitable programmes over a three-year period.Kelce has also helped fund the organisation for years. The Chiefs have reported that his contributions through personal gifts and directed funding have approached $2 million.The $35,000 award comes at a time when Eighty-Seven and Running is working to address concerns raised by a review of its federal tax records.The foundation reported spending 41 cents of every dollar on charitable activities during the latest three-year period covered by its filings. It also reported significant payments to A&A Management Group, which was co-founded by Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes.Aaron Eanes said the foundation had incorrectly categorised expenses on its tax filings for years. He said the organisation has since changed its reporting practices and eliminated management fees in 2025.“Our previous approach to categorizing expenses on our 990 filings did not accurately reflect actual fund usage,” Eanes told The Republic in a written statement.“We have since corrected this: management fees decreased significantly in 2024 and dropped to zero in 2025,” Eanes said.The foundation also plans to expand its board and add nonprofit advisers.For Kelce, sending the latest prize to an established charity provides a direct route for the money to reach its intended beneficiaries while his own foundation works through those changes.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce directs $35,000 prize to Operation Breakthrough. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end won the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Charity Challenge for the third time. The decision came as his foundation Eighty-Seven and Running faced questions over its financial reporting, governance and spending.

Article Title: Ricky Hatton’s £30m estate: Son Campbell says family is ‘completely in the dark’ as questions grow over the late boxer’s finances
Article Text:
Ricky Hatton (via Getty)

Ricky Hatton’s £30m estate and business assets

Ricky Hatton’s £1.5m house sold after his death

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ricky Hatton’s family is still waiting for clarity over the former boxing champion’s finances, more than a year after his death. New figures suggest Hatton left an estate worth around £30 million, built through his boxing career, businesses and property investments. But his son Campbell Hatton says the family has had little information about what happened to the money. Campbell told The Sun: “My family is still completely in the dark. We’ve had no involvement in my dad’s finances for over 15 years.” Trustees were appointed to handle the estate, but questions over its distribution remain.Hatton, who died aged 46 in September 2025, built much of his wealth during a successful boxing career. He later put money into businesses and property, with the latest figures putting the value of his business interests at more than £20 million and property investments at around £10 million. These figures are estimates based on company accounts and reported property holdings, rather than a confirmed amount that his children will receive.Companies House records showed around 20 businesses linked to Hatton when he died.One of them, DHT Finance Limited, was valued at more than £18 million, while CWR 2021 Limited was worth almost £2.5 million. Some businesses, however, had liabilities. RHHP Limited was reported to have net liabilities of more than £2.1 million.Hatton was also linked to property investments, including a significant stake in a Leicester development valued at about £30 million. That figure refers to the development itself and should not be treated as Hatton’s personal wealth.The family’s uncertainty is linked in part to the absence of a will. Trustees were appointed to deal with the estate, but reports say communication between them and people close to Hatton’s family has become difficult. The Sun reported that one source described the situation as a “complete mess”.Hatton was understood to have wanted his wealth to provide for his three children, Campbell, 25, and daughters Millie and Fearne. However, there is still no clear public timetable for when or how the estate will be distributed.Another part of Hatton’s property holdings was his home in Gee Cross, Greater Manchester. The five-bedroom house was eventually sold for £1.5 million this year, after initially being listed for £1.85 million. The property was taken off the market after Hatton’s death and later returned with lower asking prices before the sale.The Daily Mail previously reported the £1.5 million sale, citing Land Registry records.The sale is separate from the wider £30 million estimate and does not by itself show how much money will eventually pass to Hatton’s children.For Campbell, the main issue is still knowing what his father left behind and what will happen to it. The latest reports have brought more figures into the public domain, but the family is still waiting for clearer answers about the estate.Ricky Hatton’s estate is estimated at around £30 million, with more than £20 million linked to businesses and another £10 million in property investments.His son Campbell says the family is still “completely in the dark” about the finances. Trustees are handling the estate, while Hatton’s former home has been sold for £1.5 million.
Article Summary: Ricky Hatton’s estate is estimated at around £30 million, with more than £20 million linked to businesses and another £10 million in property investments. His son Campbell says the family is still “completely in the dark’ about the finances. Trustees are handling the estate, while Hatton's former home has been sold for £1.5 million.

Article Title: Accepted her as she was still PM: Indian envoy on Hasina's flight
Article Text:
.

TOI Correspondent from Dhaka:

Former PM Sheikh Hasina was not brought to India by the Indian air force or army, but arrived on a Bangladeshi military aircraft, and "we hardly had any choice other than accepting her as she was still Bangladesh's PM", India's high commissioner in Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, said Saturday.On Bangladesh's request for Hasina's extradition, Trivedi made it clear the legal process concerning extradition is ongoing, and no timeframe can be given as courts are involved.The Indian envoy made the remarks while responding to questions after addressing a session of the Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka, which was inaugurated by PM Tarique Rahman.Talking about the circumstances surrounding Hasina's arrival in India following her government's fall in Aug 2024, Trivedi said that "at that point in time, Hasina was still PM". "We had hardly any choice on that. It was our duty as a neighbour to accept the reality of life, because situations are such where at times you are not prepared for it," said Trivedi, who was appointed high commissioner in April this year."What was our choice? If you had said that no, we are not going to accept, we don't give landing permission. Things would have been I don't know what," Trivedi said, adding, "Indian authorities were not prepared for the situation."The situation unfolded because of "tragic circumstances" in Bangladesh at that time, he said, and stressed, "Hasina was not brought to India by the Indian air force or army."On Hasina's extradition, Trivedi said that "again and again, the Indian government has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured. So, as far as that is concerned, the process is on." He said the courts are involved in the matter and therefore "nobody can give you a timeframe."Trivedi underscored that India's relationship with Bangladesh does not depend on Dhaka's relations with other countries. He stressed that both countries have the right to protect their respective national interests.Trivedi highlighted the need for continuous dialogue, mutual respect and trust between Bangladesh and India to address bilateral issues, saying every issue between the two neighbours has a solution. He acknowledged that the process of engagement between the countries may be slow, but it has not stopped. "I can guarantee you, there is no stoppage of the process. The process is ongoing," Trivedi said.
Article Summary: Former PM Sheikh Hasina was not brought to India by the Indian air force or army, but arrived on a Bangladeshi military aircraft. "We hardly had any choice other than accepting her as she was still Bangladesh's PM", India's high commissioner in Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, said.

Article Title: A year on, Bengaluru-Mumbai superfast train promise remains on paper
Article Text:
Despite a promise made a year ago by the Railway Minister, no superfast train service exists between Bengaluru and Mumbai

TOI





BENGALURU: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters for years.On Sept 27, 2025, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya announced through his X account that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured him of a superfast train connecting the two cities. Twelve months later, however, the promised train has not started.For passengers, the situation has changed little. For over three decades, Udyan Express has remained the only daily direct service between Bengaluru and Mumbai that takes roughly 24 hours to cover the journey.There was some movement in May 2026, when railways introduced a bi-weekly SMVT Bengaluru-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express. But the additional service did not address the central demand for a faster connection: that train too takes around 24 hours.The next assurance raised expectations further. In May, Vaishnaw tolda Vande Bharat sleeper service on Bengaluru-Mumbai route will be introduced in Aug. That, too, has not materialised.The railway board subsequently allocated a rake that had initially been planned for Bengaluru-Mumbai route to Northern Railway zone, leaving passengers without a launch date for the proposed service.Rail users from across Karnataka have taken to social media to question the delay. Karnataka Rail Users sarcastically marked the first anniversary of the announcement, while other passenger groups accused the Centre and South Western Railway (SWR) zone of making promises without delivering the service.Mahendra Singhi, a member of SWR’s Zonal Railway Users’ Consultative Committee in Hubballi, said the railway board should introduce a Vande Bharat on the route to provide the speed and comfort passengers have been seeking.The BJP’s Karnataka migrant outreach network has also sought an early decision. “Nearly a year has passed since the announcement, yet there has been no official communication regarding the launch date of this service. The train will significantly benefit passengers and strengthen connectivity between Bengaluru, the IT capital of India, and Mumbai, the financial capital,“ Bharat Jain, co-convener (Karnataka), BJP Rajasthani Pravasi Prakoshth, stated.
Article Summary: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion. It plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses.

Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.

Article Title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
Article Text:
About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia (AI Image)





CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure.“It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful. ”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. So, this is an important part of the action plan to make Tamil Nadu a dementia-aware state,” says Ramani.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. More than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed. The state is looking at making the condition a ‘public health priority’

Article Title: Military-grade drones worth Rs 1 crore seized at Delhi airport
Article Text:
The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.





NEW DELHI: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.During Customs proceedings, the passengers were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 11 remote controllers of autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers, 20 data cables, 40 remote controller joysticks and other parts. They also recovered one iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 GB.“Chartered engineer informed Customs officers that these are professional-grade drones with thermal imaging and laser range-finder and are military/defence grade UAV. They also require mandatory DGCA registration for each drone. The total market value was assessed at Rs 1 crore,” said a Customs official.The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.“One passenger also stated that he intentionally smuggled these drones into India without declaration to the Customs authorities and without payment of applicable Customs duty,” said the official.
Article Summary: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam. They were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers and 20 data cables.

Article Title: Google data center head says that there are 'hundreds of thousands' of skilled trade jobs across the US as the company launches commitment to help 25,000 ...
Article Text:
A personal story behind the push

What the commitment includes

Why the need is so urgent

Part of a broader pattern of investment

Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers, as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the AI-driven data center boom. Tim Chadwick, Google’s Data Center Operations Area Lead, says there are “hundreds of thousands” of skilled trade jobs open across the country right now. Data centers have become central to the AI economy, requiring massive investment and labor. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the U.S., ranging from master electricians to project managers. These jobs offer long-term stability and high wages, but employers face challenges in recruiting due to decades of emphasis on four-year degrees over vocational training.The announcement was written by Tim Chadwick, Google's Data Center Operations Area lead for Ohio and Indiana, who shared his own path from military service into the tech industry. Chadwick spent seven years as a nuclear-trained operator in the US Navy and another 13 years as a submarine officer before transitioning to civilian life — a shift he described as genuinely difficult, one he credits his professional network with helping him navigate.A former shipmate ultimately helped him land an interview for a role managing data center engineering operations.Chadwick noted that many of the skills built while running a nuclear submarine — planning and leading a mission, working closely with technicians, and exercising sound judgment under pressure — translate directly into overseeing data center operations, a connection that shaped his interest in helping other veterans find similar paths.Google.org's funding and support will flow to three organizations with deep experience serving the veteran community: Hiring Our Heroes, Student Veterans of America (SVA), and the Home Builders Institute (HBI). Together, these organizations will offer hands-on pre-apprenticeships, career coaching, and direct job placement support aimed at helping veterans and military family members move into skilled trade careers.Chadwick pointed to the sheer scale of unmet demand driving the initiative, noting that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently open across the US, spanning positions like master electrician, lead pipefitter, and project manager. He described these as high-growth careers offering long-term financial stability — and argued that veterans and military families are especially well-suited for them, given how closely the roles align with skills many already carry from military service, including problem-solving under pressure, teamwork, and a strong drive to get a job done right.This isn't Google's first move in this space. Earlier this year, the company joined BlackRock, Ford, and Carhartt to launch the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades, aimed at building stronger pipelines into vocational careers nationally. Google.org has also previously funded the Electrical Training Alliance (etA) to bring AI-powered learning tools directly onto the trade floor, and provided a $4 million grant to Student Veterans of America to expand access to Google Career Certificates and AI training for veterans nationwide.Today's announcement is also part of Google.org's broader AI Opportunity Fund for the United States, an initiative aimed at ensuring Americans across different career paths can benefit from advances in AI technology, rather than being left behind by them.
Article Summary: Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers. The initiative comes as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the AI-driven data center boom. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the U.S.

Article Title: OpenAI DevDay opens with protest outside venue; protesters in robot costumes chant: 'Sam Altman, get...'
Article Text:
More than a dozen groups backed the DevDay protest

Altman's name drew boos from the crowd

Pressure on OpenAI has been building for months

OpenAI's annual DevDay conference began with a protest outside the venue in San Francisco. Demonstrators marched in a circle chanting "Sam Altman, get off it, put people over profit" as attendees arrived for the opening keynote, The Verge reported.The rally, held outside Fort Mason, was aimed mainly at OpenAI's contract with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its wider military and government work. Protesters also raised the environmental cost of data centres and the growing power of AI companies, on a day OpenAI planned to show off more than 20 products to roughly 2,500 attendees.According to The Verge, the rally was sponsored by Bay Resistance, Tech Workers Coalition, Service Employees International Union, San Francisco Rising and the San Francisco Labor Council. Large letters spelling out "People over profit" stood in front of the marchers, and a big orange sign told OpenAI to drop the ICE contract.Several protesters wore cardboard robot costumes and waved cardboard scythes. Other signs warned against killer robots working for ICE and against climate destruction. One asked where OpenAI's "moral codex" was, a dig at its Codex coding tool.A protest leader told onlookers the group would stay until Altman arrived for the keynote.Every mention of his name was met with boos, and one person shouted "Fascist!" Chants tied ICE to OpenAI's software, including a line about no more coding for ICE crimes.At one point, a protester with a loudspeaker addressed OpenAI employees directly and led a song urging them to change their minds and walk away from the company.Flyers handed out at the rally pointed people to QuitGPT.org and asked them to sign a "democracy pledge" to end ICE and military contracts. The flyer claimed OpenAI was building tools for ICE violence and that its top executives were helping fund the political rise of the MAGA movement. Another flyer marked out "safe distances" from data centres and suggested that only 100 miles or more was safe.The Verge described the protest as part of a bipartisan movement against the concentration of power in the AI industry and the lack of government regulation. QuitGPT, which says it began in February, claims about four million people have joined its boycott of ChatGPT. That figure comes from the group itself.Trust in AI also appears to be low. On Monday, OpenAI apologised for its models gaining unauthorised access to Australian government websites earlier this year, and said it had pulled plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns.Inside the venue, Altman opened the keynote by saying he expected it to be OpenAI's best DevDay yet. The company went on to announce Dots, its always-on AI agents, and a new Pro tier.
Article Summary: Demonstrators marched in a circle chanting "Sam Altman, get off it, put people over profit" The rally was aimed mainly at OpenAI's contract with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement and its wider military and government work. Protesters also raised the environmental cost of data centres and the growing power of AI companies.
